title: Observable shim: lightweight request slab + cross-framework propagator
creator: Ethan Liu
description:
Goal: Provide a low-allocation instrumentation shim for server and client SDKs that establishes a compact per-request 'slab' (fixed slot metadata) and a cross-framework propagator compatible with async/await, worker pools, and callback-based frameworks. This ticket implements the core SDK hooks and the middleware adapters for Node (Express/Fastify), Python (ASGI/WSGI), and the Go HTTP client/server wrapper.

Background: Current tracing integrations allocate per-stage context objects and perform header parsing that increases tail latency for high-concurrency workloads. We need a minimal footprint approach that: 1) reserves a tiny request slab at ingress, 2) normalizes propagation headers into a compact 4-field slab (trace_id, span_id, sampled, flags), 3) exposes non-blocking attach/detach hooks to runtime frameworks, and 4) falls back cleanly to existing full-featured propagation when a customer opts in.

Design summary:
- Request slab: 32-byte fixed struct stored in a runtime-managed pool (slot id encoded as 16-bit index). Slots are recycled after request completion; slot id is the only allocation per-request for fast paths.
- Propagator: single header namespace 'x-rdwd-prop' that carries base64-compact slab; middleware will also accept legacy headers (traceparent, x-b3-*) and translate them to slab on ingress.
- SDK hooks: small API surface: createRequestSlot(), attachSlot(slotId), detachSlot(slotId), setAttribute(key,value), getAttribute(key). Implementations are non-blocking and avoid mutex hot paths by using per-thread freelist where supported.
- Cross-language compatibility: binary slab format documented in Confluence; adapters implement safe conversion for Python async_contextvars, Node AsyncLocalStorage, and Go context.Context.

Acceptance criteria:
- Server middleware sets a slot on ingress for Node/Python/Go and attaches slot id to outgoing requests made via SDK HTTP client wrappers.
- End-to-end trace continuity across service boundary with no more than 1 allocation per request in the fast path.
- Benchmarks show <3% p95 latency regression under 5k RPS for typical 512B payloads vs baseline instrumentation.
- Dashboard shows new metrics: slab_alloc_rate, slab_reuse_ratio, propagate_fallback_rate.

Telemetry & dashboarding: Integrate slab metrics into the metrics pipeline. Create a new latency/error dashboard (template link below) showing the delta between services that use slab propagation vs legacy. Add an alert when propagate_fallback_rate > 2% for 10m.

API compatibility & rollout: Feature gate 'obs.slab_propagator' default off for GA. Offer opt-in via SDK config and Runtime route header mapping. Plan phased rollout: internal dogfood -> canary customers -> wide rollout.

Migration notes: When legacy headers are present, middleware will decode and populate the slab to avoid breaking existing traces. If both legacy and 'x-rdwd-prop' present, prefer explicit 'x-rdwd-prop'.

Security considerations: slab is compact but contains trace identifiers only; do not include PII. Optionally sign header with HMAC in Private deployments (will be separate ticket).

References: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/observable-shim-design; spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/observable-slab-spec; dashboard template: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/obs/trace-latency
comments: 2025-01-10 - Kickoff: scoped API surface and agreed on slab concept during design review. Action: spike allocation strategy (Maya).
2025-01-13 - Spike results: slot-based allocation reduces per-request allocations from 7 -> 1 in Node prototype. p95 improved in microbench. Recorded results in Confluence.
2025-01-14 - Design decision: use single compact header 'x-rdwd-prop' for fastpath; accept legacy headers for grace period.
2025-01-16 - Implementation: added Node middleware and AsyncLocalStorage attach/detach. Python ASGI shim implemented with contextvars bridge.
2025-01-18 - QA: unit tests for slot recycling and header translation added. Found edge case with streaming responses where detach happened before stream end; patch submitted.
2025-01-19 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4823 (core sdk + node middleware). Requesting frontend review from @rafael and perf review from @sophia.
2025-01-21 - Perf run: integration harness shows slab_reuse_ratio 98% under 2k RPS. Preparing canary rollout plan.
2025-01-21 - Next: implement Go wrappers and create canary config under runtime-1.22. Planning follow-up ticket for HMAC signing in private deployments.
